newsitem.title: ITALY: Dollar rise vs lira no inflation threat - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rise vs lira no inflation threat - Ciampi.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the rise of the dollar against the lira did not help Italy but it did not pose a threat to the country's inflation rate.

Ciampi, interviewed in daily newspaper La Repubblica, said: "A dollar at 1,800 lire doesn't help us but if you have a look at the fundamental economic data you can see clearly, as all the internal variables show, that the process of slowdown in inflation is not at all under debate."
The dollar touched 1,800.04 lire on Monday, its highest level for about 12 years, and was quoted at 1,790.90/2.40 by 0715 GMT on Tuesday.

"If there is going to be an international impact on our prices that won't cause a return to an inflationary spiral because the trend to converge towards the Maastricht criteria is a structural reality in our economy," Ciampi told La Repubblica.
"You will see that there won't be divergences from the fundamental trend in our inflation," he said when asked if he saw an upturn in consumer prices in coming months.

Asked if the dollar's rise could eventually cause currency tensions, force the German central bank to put up interest rates and create problems for the Italian economy, Ciampi said: "Let's avoid going from excessive optimism to seeing imminent catastrophes."

"For the moment I don't see tensions on interest rates and it seems to me the markets have also taken on board the willingness of all the countries in Europe, including Germany, to reach monetary union on time," he said.
